claim: The 円 card gives only the reading en, although this same chapter teaches 円い as marui, so the kanji card never shows that 円 also reads maru.
evidence: Reading back of 円: 'Answer: Yen; circle / Says: en'. Card r-c95956a5c8b5: '円い / Answer: Round / Says: marui'. Other kanji cards list both kinds of reading, e.g. Lesson 12's 甘 'Says: kan / ama'.
fix: Add the kun reading so the back reads 'en / maru', as other kanji cards with a used kun reading do.
verdictReason: Not a character card. The book's table prints 円(えん) 'circle' as a word, so by the deck's Japanese rule (readingSchemes.js: a single kanji the book also teaches as a word is ONE item, the word, with its reading and audio) r-c257210e5fc3 is a word card: ttsText えん, pronunciation 'en', voiced. 甘 'kan / ama' is a character card (no ttsText, silent), a different convention. Word cards for single kanji never list character readings anywhere in the deck: 人 (chapter-5) says only 'hito', 百 and 千 here say only hyaku / sen. Faithful to the rule and to its peers; changing it is a design change to all four, not a card fix.

fix: Card 子ども "Child" (reading こども) in this chapter and drop the chapter-20 duplicate, or leave it in chapter-20 and reword the exclusion reason to say so.
verdictReason: Facts check out (no 子ども card in chapter-16; 17.xhtml prints it once, inside 子どもの時; r-7957f0414249 is in chapter-20) but it is not a gap. The premise is wrong: the book prints 子供 in kanji from Lesson 4 (6.xhtml) on, and before this unit the learner has 子 'Child' (chapter-4, r-219e08c96026) and 子供 'Child' (chapter-5, r-11fb5d289abc). The word is carded in the collection; the exclusion reason is the owner's 2026-10-13 ruling and is true. Moving a delivered chapter-20 note here would be a scheduling migration for a variant spelling of a word already known; rewording a hidden provenance field changes nothing the learner sees.
